note: Test reply: letters over three days, sources, contradictory sightings, answers to T0-1 and T0-3. Illustrative. Also: an overheard exchange, an intercepted letter in cipher, a captured order.

remarks: Count Starhemberg was not pleased to learn of your inquiry into the chests from a clerk rather than from you.
The two reports of Prussian regiments cannot both be right; the merchant has been wrong before.

starhemberg: The player asked for the Hofkammer accounts through a clerk, not in person.

hidden.chronicle: Test chronicle: the first answers reach Vienna; the frontier reports disagree.

decisions.knows: The Emperor is dead; Vienna is in mourning and short of money.
decisions.decides: Keeps his counsel and orders the regiments readied, quietly.

reports.title: Three accounts, not one
reports.text: The Hofkammer separates what is promised, what the estates have granted and what lies in the chests. The last is the smallest figure by far.

reports.title: Regiments at Crossen
reports.text: A Breslau merchant swears he saw Prussian regiments in quarters about Crossen, more than he could count.

reports.title: Nothing at Crossen
reports.text: Our hussar patrol rode to within sight of Crossen and found the usual garrison only. The regiments are said to be nearer Berlin.

sighting.what: Prussian regiments, said to be near Berlin

reports.title: Boats at Linz
reports.text: Forty-one boats are counted at Linz and held; the boatmen ask who will pay their hire.

reports.title: To Berlin, by the Prussian envoy's courier
reports.text: The court is in mourning and in disorder. The old ministers quarrel; the treasury is empty; Silesia has no army. If His Majesty means to act, the season will not be kinder in the spring.
reports.source: taken from the envoy's courier at the Moravian border

reports.title: An order found at Crossen
reports.text: One of our people brought me a copy of an order posted at Crossen. I send it as it is; make of it what you will.
reports.source: a copy made by an innkeeper's son

enclosure.title: An order to the magistrates of Crossen (copy)
enclosure.text: Quarters, forage and bread are to be held ready for regiments on the march, against the end of next month.

overheard.line: …and Neipperg will have the Silesian command before Christmas, mark me — the Grand Duke has already asked for him.

changes.title: Three accounts and two rumours
changes.briefing: The first answers come in: the treasury is thinner than promised, and the frontier reports disagree.
